title: Interconnect saturation sweep - empirical results and notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick empirical sweep to understand where interconnect limits show up for our inference serving runtime when moving from single-node NVLink-bound configs to cross-node InfiniBand (IB) + GPUDirect flows. Goal: produce actionable mitigations for production Dedicated racks (A100/H100 mixes) and guidance for Private deployments.

Summary / headline findings (short):
- Same-node NVLink moves huge bulk of heavy-model KV exchange; saturation visible on large tensor-parallel allreduce and KV checkpoint broadcast at high batch/seq combos.
- Cross-node (IB HDR/200) with GPUDirect/RDMA gives decent bandwidth but higher latency and markedly larger CPU involvement for small/irregular message shapes; NCCL microbenchmarks optimistic vs real app patterns.
- Pipeline-parallel schedules that create many medium-sized collectives suffer the most when crossing nodes; tensor-parallel ring allreduce performs better across nodes if messages are large and contiguous.
- Practical ops: enforce topology-aware placement + we should enable hierarchical collectives (intra-node NVLink then inter-node IB) and add runtime heuristics that switch between algorithms based on message sizes and model shape.

Testbed and methodology (notes):
- Hardware tested: 4x DGX-style nodes, each with 8x A100 40GB (NVLink3 mesh), Mellanox HDR200 InfiniBand Cables, driver stack: NVIDIA driver 535.x, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.15, UCX 1.13. (Mixed runs with H100 planned but not included in sweep).
- Software: PyTorch 2.2 nightly, custom serving runtime branch (perf/ib-sweep), model runner instrumented with per-collective timers (start/end hooks) and async tracing to record overlap of compute/comm.
- Workloads: GPT-like transformer decoder-only models (7B, 13B, 70B) with varying TP x PP layouts; inference configs: seq_len=512/2048, batch_size=1/4/16, temperature 0.0 synthetic prompts to measure steady-state token throughput.
- Measurement artifacts: per-token latency histogram, per-collective (allreduce, broadcast, scatter, gather) wall-time, CCU (CPU% on host), PCIe memcpy time, NCCL debug logs.
- Microbenchmarks: nccl-tests bandwidth/p2p/allreduce with message sizes 1KB..256MB to map algorithms.

Representative runs (selected):
1) 70B model: TP=8, PP=1, single-node (all GPUs colocated) 
   - seq=512, batch=4:  token throughput ~9.8 tokens/s/GPU (aggregated ~78 tokens/s across 8 GPUs), per-step allreduce median 6.2 ms, NVLink aggregate near-saturation for KV exchange windows.
   - Observed NCCL transport: intra-node paths used SHM+NVLink, ring algorithm.

2) 70B model: TP=8 split across 2 nodes (4 GPUs per node) 
   - seq=512, batch=4: throughput degraded ~32% vs single-node. Per-step inter-node allreduce median 18-25 ms depending on placement.
   - CPU% increased (host process pinned threads) during collectives; trace shows extra memcpy loops and fallback to IB transport in multiple message fragments.

3) 13B model: TP=2, PP=2 across 2 nodes 
   - seq=2048, batch=1: pipeline bubble patterns dominate; when pipeline stage boundary crosses node boundary, overall latency 2.1x larger vs single-node equivalent.
   - Frequent small (<=64KB) collectives cause high latency tail.

Microbenchmark observations (nccl-tests):
- For p2p/allreduce large messages (>4MB) IB+GPUDirect bandwidth reaches ~80-90% of single-node NVLink aggregate for that subset of GPUs (numbers vary with topology).
- For mid-size messages (64KB - 2MB) throughput drops dramatically on cross-node runs; latency increases nonlinearly due to fragmentation + CPU interaction in our current UCX/NCCL settings.
- Small messages (<64KB) dominated by latency; inter-node overheads make many small collectives expensive.

Root causes and hypotheses (evidence-backed):
- Topology mismatch: our placement often spreads a tensor-parallel group across nodes by default. When TP across nodes, every step needs allreduce over the KV cache and parameter grads (for training) or key-value shuffles (for inference), causing many large messages that must use IB.
- Algorithm selection: NCCL chooses algorithms by message size, but our message shapes in model runtime are variable and often broken into fragments by internal buffering logic. These fragmented messages frequently pick suboptimal algorithms for cross-node paths.
- CPU/host involvement: UCX and NCCL path handling for RDMA requires some host orchestration in our stack; trace shows host memcpy/pinning spikes that add latency for mid-sized messages.
- PCIe & NVLink overlap: when transfers require crossing PCIe (e.g., fallback paths, host-based staging), we lose NVLink advantages and see throughput collapse.

Immediate actionable mitigations (easy -> medium effort):
- Topology-aware scheduler: prefer placing TP partitions within the same node; avoid splitting a TP group across nodes unless unavoidable. (Low effort, high win for Dedicated racks).
- NCCL env tuning: try NCCL_ALGO=Ring for large-message regimes, set NCCL_BUFFSIZE to align with our average message sizes, enable NCCL_P2P for same-node fast paths. Add env toggles in runtime config. (Low-medium effort).
- Increase aggregation in runtime: coalesce many small collectives into fewer larger messages where semantics permit (e.g., batched KV flush). (Medium effort in runtime).
- Use hierarchical allreduce (intra-node then inter-node): implement an explicit two-phase collective for our largest communication phases. (Medium-high effort).

Longer-term / research items (higher effort):
- GPUDirect/UCX tuning and newer NCCL versions: test NCCL 2.17+ and UCX 1.14+; firmware driver upgrades may change observed behaviour.
- Explore HW placement constraints for Dedicated offerings: offering a "topology-guaranteed" option for high-throughput workloads (all TP GPUs in same node or within a NVLink domain).
- Adaptive comm scheduler: runtime that samples message shapes and flips strategies (hierarchical vs direct) dynamically.
- Investigate H100 NVLink LLI behaviour (larger aggregate bandwidth) to see if cross-node penalty reduces relatively.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-ups):
- Re-run sweep with H100 nodes and with IB firmware updated; check if mid-size fragmentation problem remains.
- Measure impact of enabling CUDA IPC aggressively for same-node peer transfers in the runtime branch.
- Add automated tests in perf harness that simulate our runtime's message fragmentation pattern to guide NCCL/UCX tuning.
- Ticket: JIRA-7892 assigned to Aisha to own hierarchical collectives prototype.

Logs and artifacts location:
- Raw logs and traces: internal-shared:/bench/2025-01-22/sweep-logs.tgz
- nccl-tests raw CSVs: internal-shared:/bench/2025-01-22/nccl-microbench.csv

Appendix: quick checklist for a follow-up triage run:
- [ ] Upgrade NCCL to 2.17 candidate build + record nccl-tests baseline.
- [ ] Re-run 70B TP=8 single-node vs 2-node, with NCCL_ALGO=Ring vs Tree vs Collnet to compare tails.
- [ ] Instrument UCX to log transport selection per collective; capture host memcpy durations.
- [ ] Try coalescing small KV broadcasts in runtime (patch branch perf/kv-coalesce) and measure changes to tail latency.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working capture of the sweep; many traces are big and live in the artifacts path above. Some conclusions are preliminary but consistent across multiple runs. Please comment on the placement policy change (low-hanging) and whether we want to expose topology preferences to customers in Dedicated configs.

-- Evan
